scope: Development candidate for large recoverable prefixes and fewer simultaneous requests; no GPU or task-correctness acceptance yet.
decode_batch_semantics: The current native scheduler decodes its admitted running batch; its upper bound is also 8, with no separately tuned decode slice.

primary_comparison_policy.cutoff: earlier arm depletion below threshold after final arrival
primary_comparison_policy.incomplete_work: retain through common cutoff in restricted JCT

capacity_estimate.semantics: Logical independent-source estimate before growth and radix sharing. Waiting roots and children can exceed HBM capacity; this is not an observed residency or transfer measurement.

acceptance_observations: Actual native prompt length distribution by root, child and nested child; target a majority above 100000 tokens.
Tool-call counts, durations and LLM turns per ordinary agent; long supplied context alone does not establish a tool-intensive workload.
Observed delegation rounds, nested spawn and JOIN counts; no fixed minimum-step termination guard.
Positive Host-only FULL opportunities, actual D2H/H2D and request-critical restore waits.
Useful Host-only copy loss, same-session prefix recomputation and baseline environment blockers.
Common tail-excluded restricted workflow JCT and throughput, with full-run tails and failures retained.
interpretation: LoCoBench-Agent uses generated software projects. This is an adapted multi-agent workload rather than an official benchmark score.
Complete project source is supplied to every workstream without padding; reference answers are excluded.
Lower concurrency may reduce pressure and does not guarantee more exposed H2D or a speedup.
Interaction density and actual large-prefix restoration must be established before adopting this candidate as the primary performance workload.
